verdicts.note: Two-term elected sheriff with 36 years in the office [S1][S2][S3] against a first-time candidate: an elected department head's enacted record, -2 high holds.
'Taxes are always going to be a last resort'; revenue should come from growth [S4]. One explicit statement: -1 medium holds.

Backs the county's hiring and position freezes as a short-term step and long-term restructuring 'for the smaller county' [S4], and stresses fiscal responsibility [S1]. His support for a shelter built partly with public funds [S4] is narrow and does not reverse the direction. -1 medium holds.
No elected office; runs on 'experience outside the political system' [S1][S2] against a 36-year county official. +2 high holds.

Checked against the sources: strip county permitting and regulation to state minimums [S3], a 30-minute counter approval path and rural clustering [S2], end the well-metering requirement for building permits [S1][S2][S4], and 'People Must Live in Cities ... I say no!' [S1]. Deregulate-and-build is pole_a; repeated across three independent sources, so -2 high holds.

Would reduce county staff, reduce overall infrastructure expenditure and liquidate the water-resource system's water rights into the general fund (Herald-Republic interview, S4). One interview source but several concrete cuts: -2 medium holds.
